clue.text: Set record — first for a medical specialist!

parts.note: a radio is a wireless set
a log is a written record
1st, written out as IST

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a doctor who has broken a record by coming first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb with 'record' as its object, but it is a wireless set; 'first' is 1ST with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who interprets X-rays and scans is a recognised medical specialist.

clue.text: Amazing certain people after a hollow welcome

indicators.note: the certain people come after the hollow welcome
a hollow word has its insides removed, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: some, as in 'some say', means certain people

explanation.surface: Some people are remarkable even though they were greeted half-heartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives of strong admiration, synonyms for something that inspires wonder.

clue.text: Shanghai journalist is deeply affected

parts.note: to shanghai is to force someone into service, as a press gang did; impressing sailors meant the same
ED, short for editor, a crossword stock journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter from the Chinese city is greatly moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shanghai' reads as the city but is the verb meaning to kidnap into naval service.
explanation.definitionFit: Being moved or struck by something strongly is a synonym, as in feeling deeply touched.

clue.text: Stretched out in the air, topless

indicators.note: without its top, so the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: flying means aloft, in the air

explanation.surface: Someone sunbathing with no top on, stretched out under the open sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Being horizontal at full length, as on a bed, is a synonym of reclining.

clue.text: Chivalrous worker bears insolence

parts.note: gall means cheek or impudence
an ant is the crossword's stock worker, from the worker ant

explanation.surface: A courteous employee puts up with rudeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a man who is courteous and brave toward women, synonyms from knightly ideals.

clue.text: Genuine evil about to engulf Church

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the church letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: sin is wickedness
re means concerning, about
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Real wickedness is about to swallow up the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean honest and unfeigned, synonyms for feelings truly held.

clue.text: Firm docked one's time, after bill for musician

indicators.note: the firm and the rest come after the bill

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: docked like a tail, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a company is a firm
one is I, so one's (one is) is IS

explanation.surface: A company cut an employee's hours after receiving an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: The player who supports a soloist or singer, often on piano, is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Laugh in front of the Queen! That's a warning

indicators.note: the laugh goes before the queen

parts.note: a hoot is a loud laugh
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Someone guffaws in front of the monarch and is told off.
explanation.definitionFit: A horn or siren sounds an alert, so the device stands for a warning signal.

clue.text: Fail in competition and refuse to talk

indicators.note: the failure sits inside the competition

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition
to lose is to fail

explanation.surface: A sore loser in a tournament who then won't speak to anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To clam up is an idiom for falling silent and saying nothing more.

clue.text: Popular guy touring North, away from the sea

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the lad goes round the north

parts.note: a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A well-liked man travels around the north, away from the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a region lying in the interior of a country, far from any coast.

clue.text: Items requiring unusual smooth finishes

parts.note: odd means strange, unusual
to sand is to smooth with sandpaper
ends are finishes

explanation.surface: Pieces of furniture that need an unusual polished finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means miscellaneous small items or leftovers, so it loosely stands for assorted articles.

clue.text: Result revealed company limits of malaise

parts.note: out means exposed, made known

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A finding shows that the firm is suffering a general unease.
explanation.definitionFit: The consequence or end product of events is a synonym of what they lead to.

clue.text: Proceed at once from Indian state capital

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast
the head is the top, like the capital of a column

explanation.surface: An instruction to set off immediately from the main city of an Indian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' wants to be a city, joining 'Indian state capital'; it is the head, the top of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an imperative telling someone to start, a direct idiom for go forward now.

clue.text: Unadulterated English strain

parts.note: pure means unmixed, unadulterated

explanation.surface: A pure English breed or variety of plant or animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' reads as a noun, a breed; it is the verb, to press food through a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing cooked food through a sieve makes a smooth pulp, so the verb is a synonym of sieve.

clue.text: Unwilling to work without a dress?

definitions.meaning: a shift is a simple loose dress, so lacking one is the humorous second reading

explanation.definitionFit: Lazy and lacking drive is the standard sense; the question mark flags a jokey split into a garment plus a suffix meaning lacking.

clue.text: Person desperately wanting a night out?

definitions.text: Person desperately wanting a night out?

parts.words: Person desperately wanting a night out?
parts.note: reads as a party-goer craving an evening on the town, but means someone longing for a night's sleep, a night spent out cold

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot sleep lies awake longing to be unconscious for the night, the pun on being out.

clue.text: Meat that's cooked inside doesn't mostly spread worms!

indicators.note: the cooked meat goes inside the other piece
spread out means scattered, so these letters are rearranged too
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

indicators.note: cooked means altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that meat which is cooked doesn't really spread parasitic worms.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'doesn't' is ignored; 'mostly' leaves DOESN, which 'spread' makes NODES, and 'cooked' gives EMAT to sit 'inside' after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundworms form a large group of the creatures, so the answer names a kind of worm.

clue.text: Quantity produced by factory with one working?

parts.note: a mill is a factory
I is the Roman numeral one
on means operating, working

explanation.surface: How much a factory turns out with a single machine running.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand thousand is a number, so it stands for a quantity, a little loosely.

clue.text: Let out to cover study for mechanism

indicators.note: to cover means to go round, so the rearranged letters surround the study
out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A room is let out to cover the cost of a study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' gives TLE, split in two so 'to cover' can wrap it round the study word.
explanation.definitionFit: The foot pedal that drives a sewing machine or lathe is an example of a simple mechanism.

clue.text: Another one's bird?

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the phrase has the bird inside it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bird belongs to someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-legged wading bird of riversides is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Waits for operator to suspend lad

parts.note: to hang is to suspend
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone stays on the line for the switchboard to ban a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying on the phone line, as when waiting to be connected, is the idiom meaning holding the line.

clue.text: Engineers turn up impressive formula

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: epic means grand, impressive

explanation.surface: Engineers arrive with a remarkable formula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reads like 'arrive', but it reverses EPIC in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of instructions for making a dish is a formula, a synonym in the kitchen.

clue.text: Sun and Express may be financially sound

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
to vent feelings is to express them

explanation.surface: Two British tabloid newspapers, the Sun and the Express, might be in good financial shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make the Sun and the Express look like newspapers; they are Sol and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm able to pay its debts is described this way, the accountant's word for financially healthy.

clue.text: Wooden serving dish (non-U!)

indicators.note: non-U, literally not U, means the letter U is dropped; it is also a term for unrefined usage

parts.note: a tureen is a deep dish for serving soup

explanation.surface: A soup dish made of wood, judged not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' was a mid-century British label for words used by the lower classes; here it removes U.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for things made of wood, used as an adjective meaning made of timber.

clue.text: Handcuff chap, adult, oddly calmed

parts.note: a man is a chap
A is the film certificate for adult

indicators.note: oddly means taking the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Cuffing a man, a grown-up who strangely went quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal ring fastened around the wrist is a shackle, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Tinker's dossier covering two days

indicators.note: covering means going round, so the dossier surrounds the days

parts.note: a file is a dossier
D is the abbreviation for day, so two of them are DD

explanation.surface: A tinker's file of papers spanning a couple of days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker's' looks like a possessive; it is the verb tinker followed by 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle or fiddle about with something is to tinker, a synonym for idle adjustment.

clue.text: At home with drink, kids with no limits being tasteless

parts.note: in means at home
a sip is a small drink

indicators.note: without its limits, a word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Staying home with a drink while unruly children are dull company.
explanation.definitionFit: Food lacking flavour is bland, and the word stands for something without taste.

clue.text: Mutually destructive niece set straight by trainee doctor

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: an intern is a junior hospital doctor in training

indicators.note: setting something straight means putting it in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young doctor sets a wayward niece on the right path.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing conflict within a group that harms both sides, the dictionary sense of reciprocal damage.
